_nota: Contraparte en inglés de mission_profiles.json (2026-11-15): el nombre de cada perfil, lo que EMMA dice de cada aspecto (`statement`), las discrepancias, lo que se buscó y la indicación del apartado de cada cita. El inglés no dice más que el castellano: cada «es una estimación», «es un plan» o «no dice» sigue ahí. Las frases citadas (`quote`), los títulos y lo que el apartado copia de la página van en el idioma de la fuente y no están aquí. El fichero castellano es el que se valida y no cambia.

strings.espacio cislunar (Orion, entre la Tierra: cislunar space (Orion, between Earth and the Moon)
strings.La fuente no da una cifra de retardo. Di: The source gives no delay figure. It says that, aboard the station, the crew receives real-time guidance from Mission Control during medical procedures.
strings.Se estima que una evacuación médica desd: A medical evacuation from the station is estimated to take less than 24 hours to reach definitive care. This comes from a conference paper archived in NTRS, which takes it from an aerospace medicine handbook: it is an estimate, not a flight procedure.
strings.Las tripulaciones de la estación reciben: Station crews regularly receive supplies on cargo flights from Earth.
strings.Misiones de estación «típicas» de seis m: «Typical» station missions of six months; the same page speaks, in another section, of missions of six to twelve months.
strings.La estación orbita a 240 millas sobre la: The station orbits 240 miles above Earth.
strings.Dentro de la protección del campo magnét: Inside the protection of Earth's magnetic field: the station crew receives more radiation than on Earth, but the planet's magnetic field protects it significantly. On the solar cycle, another page says that the Sun has an 11-year cycle that culminates in a large increase in the number and intensity of flares; it does not say which phase the cycle is in today.
strings.En 24 horas, la estación da 16 vueltas a: In 24 hours, the station makes 16 orbits of Earth and passes through 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets.
strings.A bordo de la estación, la tripulación r: Aboard the station, the crew receives real-time guidance from Mission Control when it uses medical technologies to perform procedures.
strings.La luz recorre la distancia media entre: Light covers the average distance between Earth and the Moon in 1.3 seconds. That is the light time, not the communication delay: a NASA technical memorandum gives, for lunar missions, latencies of 3 to 14 seconds each way, because of the distance and the communications architecture. On the Artemis II flyby, NASA expected to lose contact with the crew for about 40 minutes while the Moon blocked the signals between the spacecraft and Earth: that is a planned outage, not a delay.
strings.Microgravedad: la nota del regreso de Ar: Microgravity: the Artemis II return release says that its AVATAR experiment studies how human tissue responds to microgravity and to the deep-space radiation environment. A 2021 NASA page described Gateway, the station then planned around the Moon, as a microgravity and deep-space environment; it is a plan, not a flight.
strings.Los trajes de Orion pueden mantener con: Orion's suits can keep the crew alive for six days if the cabin depressurizes, to cover a return of several days from the Moon. This comes from the Orion reference guide, which gives no medical evacuation time.
strings.La guía de referencia de Orion dice que: The Orion reference guide says that at the Moon the crew will not have frequent deliveries of spare parts from Earth, like those that reach the space station, and that Orion carries the consumables, such as food and water, for the whole mission. Another page says, of missions beyond low Earth orbit in general, that one challenge is meeting basic needs without resupply missions from the ground.
strings.Artemis II, un sobrevuelo lunar y el pri: Artemis II, a lunar flyby and the first crewed flight of Orion, lasted 9 days, 1 hour and 32 minutes: it is the observed duration of one flight, not a typical duration. The Orion reference guide speaks of missions of days, weeks or even months.
strings.La Luna está de media a 384.400 kilómetr: The Moon is on average 384,400 kilometers from Earth, and the Artemis II crew took about three days to arrive. At its farthest point, Artemis II took its crew 252,756 miles from Earth.
strings.Un artículo de la NASA de 2022, anterior: A 2022 NASA article, written before the uncrewed Artemis I flight, said that Orion would pass through the Van Allen belts, with two periods of intense radiation in the first hours after launch and again on return, and that outside the protection of Earth's magnetic field it would be exposed to a harsher radiation environment than that of the station, with solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays. It is a forecast, not a measurement from the flight. On the solar cycle, another page says that the Sun has an 11-year cycle that culminates in a large increase in the number and intensity of flares; it does not say which phase the cycle is in today.
strings.Los trajes de Orion pueden mantener con: Orion's suits can keep the crew alive for six days if the cabin depressurizes, to cover a return of several days from the Moon. A NASA technical memorandum says, of crewed deep-space missions in general, that there will be no viable evacuation or rescue options and that communication latency will prevent real-time operational and medical support.
strings.La luz recorre la distancia media entre: Light covers the average distance between Earth and the Moon in 1.3 seconds. That is the light time, not the communication delay: a NASA technical memorandum gives, for lunar missions, latencies of 3 to 14 seconds each way, because of the distance and the communications architecture.
strings.Gravedad parcial: en la superficie lunar: Partial gravity: on the lunar surface, about one sixth of Earth's gravity.
strings.Una evacuación médica desde la superfici: A medical evacuation from the lunar surface could require keeping a seriously ill crew member stable for up to about 14 days during the return to Earth, because of the several vehicles and orbits involved. This comes from a conference paper archived in NTRS, which takes it from another reference: it is an estimate.
strings.Ante una necesidad imprevista de un mate: Faced with an unforeseen need for a specific item, the crew might have to wait weeks or months to receive it from Earth; the article says so in a paragraph about missions to the Moon, with the example of a medication. Another page says, of missions beyond low Earth orbit in general, that one challenge is meeting basic needs without resupply missions from the ground.
strings.En Artemis IV, dos tripulantes bajarán a: On Artemis IV, two crew members will descend to the surface and spend approximately a week near the Moon's south pole. It is the plan of a mission, not an observed duration.
strings.Unas 1.000 veces más lejos de la Tierra: About 1,000 times farther from Earth than the space station. Another page speaks of «a three-day lunar trip».
strings.Fuera de la magnetosfera protectora de l: Outside Earth's protective magnetosphere, and the Moon has no magnetic field of its own. On the solar cycle, another page says that the Sun has an 11-year cycle that culminates in a large increase in the number and intensity of flares; it does not say which phase the cycle is in today.
strings.Casi toda la Luna está cubierta de regol: Almost all of the Moon is covered in regolith: fine gray dust and rock debris. On the Apollo missions, dust that had stuck to the suits during the moonwalks got into the lunar module, floated loose in the air after liftoff and irritated the crews' eyes and throats. A 2015 HRP evidence report says that the episodic exposure limit for airborne lunar dust was set at 0.3 mg/m³ for a six-month stay on the surface.
strings.En los lugares de Apollo, cerca del ecua: At the Apollo sites, near the lunar equator, there are about 14.5 Earth days of light followed by about 14.5 of night. In the polar regions the cycle is irregular and depends on the lunar seasons: some areas never receive direct sunlight and others are lit for more than 14.5 days and dark for much less time. This comes from a 2022 NASA architecture white paper.
strings.Una evacuación médica desde la superfici: A medical evacuation from the lunar surface could require the crew medical officer (CMO) to stabilize and sustain a critically ill crew member for up to about 14 days during the return to Earth. This comes from a conference paper archived in NTRS, which takes it from another reference: it is an estimate. A 2017 slide places level of care IV next to «Lunar > 30 day»: by duration, not by the destination alone.
strings.Hasta 20 minutos por sentido. La fuente: Up to 20 minutes each way. The source says it of missions to Mars and of the stay on Mars, not of the transit in particular.
strings.Ingravidez durante el trayecto entre los: Weightlessness during the trip between the planets. The same sentence says that, once on the surface of Mars, gravity is approximately one third of Earth's.
strings.Abortar en el tránsito a Marte puede tar: Aborting during Mars transit can take many months to return the crew to Earth, whatever the transportation system, and in many cases may not help in an emergency, because the return would take longer than the crew can contain it. This comes from a NASA scoping analysis, about aborting the mission and not about evacuating a sick crew member; no source read gives a medical evacuation time specific to the transit. A technical memorandum says, of deep space in general, that there are no viable evacuation or rescue options, and the standard says, in general, that return to Earth may not be possible or may take so long that it is futile.
strings.Sin los vuelos de carga que recibe la es: Without the cargo flights the station receives: those who go to Mars will have to take with them all the food, equipment and medical supplies.
strings.Un trayecto de seis meses entre los plan: A six-month trip between the planets; the round-trip mission, up to three years.
strings.Marte está, de media, a 140 millones de: Mars is, on average, 140 million miles from Earth.
strings.Fuera del campo magnético y de la atmósf: Outside the magnetic field and the atmosphere that protect Earth: the page says it of the trip to Mars. On the solar cycle, another page says that the Sun has an 11-year cycle that culminates in a large increase in the number and intensity of flares; it does not say which phase the cycle is in today.
strings.Ante la posibilidad de emergencias médic: Faced with the possibility of medical emergencies, with a delay of up to 20 minutes each way, the crew will have to handle a range of situations with minimal support from the teams on Earth; the page says it of missions to Mars. A technical memorandum says, of crewed deep-space missions in general, that communication latency prevents real-time operational and medical support. A 2017 slide places level of care V next to «Mars Expedition», and the EIMO slides speak of health systems increasingly independent of Earth for Mars-class missions.
strings.Hasta 20 minutos por sentido mientras se: Up to 20 minutes each way while on Mars.
strings.Gravedad parcial: aproximadamente un ter: Partial gravity: approximately one third of Earth's.
strings.Opciones limitadas de abortar el descens: Limited options to abort the descent and the ascent in the first human missions to Mars. The DRA 5.0 reference architecture limits Mars aborts to the start of the mission or to returns of several years; a technical memorandum says, of deep-space missions in general, that there are no viable evacuation or rescue options. Neither gives an evacuation time from the surface.
strings.Quienes vayan a Marte tendrán que llevar: Those who go to Mars will have to take with them all the food, equipment and medical supplies. The DRA 5.0 reference architecture gives one logistics delivery every 26 months.
strings.Vivir y trabajar en Marte hasta dos años: Living and working on Mars for up to two years. The DRA 5.0 reference architecture gives a stay of 495 to 540 days; it is an architecture, not the plan of a mission.
strings.Marte está, de media, a 140 millones de: Mars is, on average, 140 million miles from Earth. The DRA 5.0 reference architecture gives 58 to 400 million kilometers.
strings.Marte no tiene un campo magnético global: Mars has no global magnetic field, and its atmosphere, much thinner than Earth's, gives only minimal protection even on the surface. The source gives no dose. On the solar cycle, another page says that the Sun has an 11-year cycle that culminates in a large increase in the number and intensity of flares; it does not say which phase the cycle is in today.
strings.Durante 1.645 días marcianos, Perseveran: Over 1,645 Martian days, Perseverance measured fine and ultrafine dust stuck to samples of suit material, with particles small enough to enter the lungs and pass into the blood. Mars dust is mostly silicates and carries reactive compounds, such as perchlorates that can alter thyroid function and reactive iron that damages cells; the article says that its health risk depends on the amount of dust and the exposure time, and that its grains are less abrasive than those of the Moon. A 2015 HRP evidence report said that the work to set an exposure limit for Mars dust remained to be done.
strings.Marte da una vuelta sobre sí mismo cada: Mars turns once on its axis every 24.6 hours, very similar to Earth's day (23.9 hours); Martian days are called sols.
strings.Con un retardo de hasta 20 minutos por s: With a delay of up to 20 minutes each way, the crew will have to handle a range of situations with minimal support from the teams on Earth. A 2017 slide places level of care V next to «Mars Expedition», and the EIMO slides speak of health systems increasingly independent of Earth for Mars-class missions.
strings.Otra página de la NASA da «unas 250 mill: Another NASA page gives «about 250 miles», not 240.
strings.Un artículo de congreso archivado en NTR: A conference paper archived in NTRS gives for the Moon «up to 5-14 seconds» of latency, not 3 to 14.
strings.Un memorando técnico de la NASA dice, de: A NASA technical memorandum says, of crewed deep-space missions in general and without naming cislunar space, that there will be no viable evacuation or rescue options.
A NASA technical memorandum says, of crewed deep-space missions in general and without naming the Moon, that there will be no viable evacuation or rescue options.
strings.Un memorando técnico de la NASA da hasta: A NASA technical memorandum gives up to 22 minutes each way, not 20, at the maximum distance from Earth. A NASA Science page gives the light time between the two planets, 3 to 22 minutes depending on their position: it is light time, not the delay of a communications system, and it does not say how much the latter adds.
strings.Sobre la gravedad en la superficie de Ma: On gravity on the surface of Mars (not that of the transit), another NASA page says «three eighths» and not «one third».
strings.Otra página de la NASA da esa misma cifr: Another NASA page gives that same figure, 140 million miles, as the round trip and not as the average distance.
strings.Las fuentes de NASA no dan una sola cifr: NASA's sources do not give a single figure: those above say one third and another page says three eighths. EMMA does not choose and shows both.
strings.En el resumen ejecutivo y la introducció: In the executive summary and the introduction of the HRP evidence report on celestial dust (read on 2026-11-03), what they say about dust aboard the space station was searched for: they speak of the dust on the surface of a celestial body and of the dust that enters the return vehicle from it; no sentence read speaks of dust aboard the space station.

In the executive summary and the introduction of the HRP evidence report on celestial dust (read on 2026-11-03), what they say about dust aboard Orion was searched for: the only sentence about dust in microgravity speaks of the vehicle returning from a surface («the return vehicle»), not of Orion, and it is not applied to a spacecraft the sentence does not name.
strings.En las páginas leídas de Artemis II (la: In the Artemis II pages read (the mission page and the record and return releases) and in the Orion reference guide, «sunrise», «sunset», «sunlight», «daylight», «night» and «circadian» were searched for: they only speak of day and night on the lunar surface as seen from the spacecraft, not of the light on board.
strings.En el artículo de la NASA sobre el polvo: In the NASA article on Mars dust measured by Perseverance and in the executive summary and the introduction of the HRP evidence report on celestial dust (read on 2026-11-03), what they say about dust during the trip was searched for: they speak of the dust on the surface and of the dust that enters the habitats and vehicles from it, not of the transit.
strings.En las páginas leídas del tránsito (los: In the transit pages read (the HRP hazards of gravity and of distance), «sunrise», «sunset», «sunlight», «daylight», «night» and «circadian» were searched for: they do not speak of daylight or of night during the trip.
